text:
What Ruth knew about her grandfather came to her the way most family history
comes: from her father, who told it often. Where the records and the family part company,
this chapter says so; for Anders, no records have been consulted yet, so everything here is
the family's account.

The Calders came from Norway. Anders Calder crossed the Atlantic on a ship at sixteen, "or
that's what my father always said," Ruth added, and he did it in one pair of boots, which he
wore the whole way across. "My father loved to tell that one."

In Duluth he found work on the ore boats, loading iron ore at the docks. "That's where the
work was," Ruth said.
